newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to ask foreign banks to roll over loans.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to ask foreign banks to roll over loans.

text.p: Thai central bank governor Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi said on Tuesday Thailand needs to build confidence among the foreign financial community to ensure that it could safely roll over loans extended to Thai corporate borrowers.

"If we do not win confidence of foreign financial institutions, which play the role of lenders, and if our short-term borrowing were not rolled over or there were fast fund outflows, our country could not survive," Chaiyawat said.

He told reporters: "Although the IMF package represents our efforts to tackle our economic problems, we also need to build confidence among the international community...this is a time for confidence building."

The central bank governor said after meeting foreign bankers based in Thailand that the $16.7 billion financial bailout package that the country obtained with the help of the International Monetary Fund would not be sufficient if private foreign lenders refused to roll over loans for corporate borrowers.
Thailand has nearly $89 billion of foreign debt, of which about two thirds have been tapped by the private sector.
"We cannot expect all foreign funds to remain in Thailand. We have expected some of them to leave. But most of them should continue to stay here," he said.
Foreign banks earlier called on the authorities to help them secure repayment of loans extended to 58 cash-strapped finance and securities firms suspended by the government since late June.
Chaiyawat said his meeting with foreign bankers produced a positive result as they agreed to continue supporting Thailand by rolling over matured loans.
David Proctor, president of the Foreign Bankers Assocation, said the meeting represented a positive step of cooperation between foreign banks and the Thai authorities.
"I'm very pleased to hear the increase of transparency and to improve provision of data and information (by the authority)," Proctor said.
"In general, on behalf of the Foreign Banks Association, we look forward to working with the Bank of Thailand," he added.
